result:
Done — `Money` now normalizes to 4 decimal places.

`libs/common/src/main/java/mn/acme/common/Money.java:12`:

```java
/** Amounts are held at four decimal places so FX-denominated orders keep their precision. */
private static final int SCALE = 4;
...
this.amount = amount.setScale(SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
```

Rounding mode is unchanged (`HALF_UP`), so the only behavioral difference is that amounts keep two more digits before rounding.

Verification and reach:
- `gradle --offline test --rerun-tasks` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, both `MoneyTest` cases PASSED (they compare with `compareTo`, so they're scale-independent). The two service modules have no test sources, so they compile-only.
- Every consumer of `Money` goes through this constructor and none of them assume a scale: `OrderService.total`, `OrderEntity.total`, `InventoryService.valueOnHand`, `StockItem.unitPrice`. `plus` re-normalizes through the constructor, so sums pick up the new scale automatically.
- `origin/feature/shipping` has `ShippingService.quote`, which just passes a `Money` through — it inherits the new scale with no change needed, but that branch will need a rebase/merge to pick this up.

Two things outside the code that this change implies, which I did not touch since there's nothing in the repo for them: `Money` is embedded in JPA entities (`OrderEntity`, `StockItem`), so the underlying columns need to be widened to `DECIMAL(n,4)` — there are no migration or schema files in this repo, so that lives wherever your DDL is managed. Likewise, any API responses or persisted values produced before this change carry 2 decimals; reading them back is fine (they'll be padded), but anything comparing a stored string form to a freshly computed one will now see `1.5000` instead of `1.50`.
